ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ADB \cong \triangle ECB$, and the corresponding point of A is E, the corresponding point of D is C. If $\angle CBD = 40^\circ$ and $BD \perp EC$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle D$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let BD and EC intersect at point G,\\
since $\triangle ADB \cong \triangle ECB$,\\
it follows that $\angle C = \angle D$,\\
since BD$\perp$EC,\\
it follows that $\angle BGC = 90^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle C = \angle D = 90^\circ - \angle CBD = 90^\circ - 40^\circ = \boxed{50^\circ}$.
